Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 824
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/824
- **Title**: gh-823 [BUG][P1] gh-807 rules require './reviewVerdicts.js' — fails in pack runtime (module lives at common/) release self-test must LOAD rule files — fa ticks red again
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-823` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 23
- **Additions**: +1053
- **Deletions**: -50
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T17:24:42Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T17:24:42Z

## PR Description

Closes #823
### Root Cause

The fa ticks died with `Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js (…/packs/sm_github-0.1.38/js/reviewVerdicts.js)` whenever a conflict-shaped gh-807 query had candidates. The dmtools runtime resolves requires **by execution time** (verified with a scratch probe pack): a require that runs while a module initializes resolves **file-relative**, but a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call) resolves against the **pack's `js/` root exclusively** — a file-relative hit is never tried. The lazy `require('./reviewVerdicts.js')` in `js/common/smProvider.js` (`_verdictRecordsModule`, fired by the `latestVerdict`/`notLatestVerdict` query guards) only executed in the deferred mode → `js/reviewVerdicts.js` → miss → whole tick red. Ticks without conflict-shaped candidates never ran it — hence the intermittent four-red-ticks pattern. Five more files carried the same latent shape (`./trackers.js` fallbacks in `jiraHelpers`/`tokenUsageComment`/`validateInputJql`/`contentOutput`, deferred `../configLoader.js` in `contentOutput`). The gh-812 zip-content gate passed the release because its union model assumed the runtime also tries the file-relative base for deferred requires — it does not.

### Fix

- Hoisted every deferred require to **load time** (file-relative — the mode where the spec is correct, and what `dmtools compile` discovers for the pack closure): `js/common/smProvider.js`, `jiraHelpers.js`, `tokenUsageComment.js`, `validateInputJql.js`, `contentOutput.js`.
- The ticket's literal pack-root-relative spec (`./common/reviewVerdicts.js`) is unshippable: `dmtools compile` resolves strictly file-relative and hard-fails the build on it (verified). Installer/compiler changes are a non-goal (#375), so eliminating the deferred mode is the only shape that compiles, loads, and keeps the closure complete.
- `ci/pack_require_gate.cjs`: the release require gate now classifies each literal require as **load-time** (union of bases, unchanged) vs **deferred** (function body → js-root base **only**). Reintroducing the shipped lazy require fails the release (AC2).
- `ci/pack_load_probe.cjs` + `assertPackLoads` in `ci/release_packs.mjs`: after every pack build the zip is extracted and a generated probe **requires every packed `.js` in the real dmtools runtime** — parse errors and load-time misses fail the release.
- `AGENTS.md`: the require-timing model documented as a coding constraint.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` (new): pins the resolution model, asserts the incident modules carry **zero deferred requires** (a re-lazied require turns it red), replays the verdict-record chain end-to-end through the provider.
- `js/unit-tests/test_packRequireGate.js`: deferred-require suites incl. the red-team replay of the shipped flat require → gate red; the pre-fix tree flags exactly the 8 shipped deferred requires, the fixed tree 0.

# gh-823: [BUG][P1] gh-807 rules require './reviewVerdicts.js' — fails in pack runtime (module lives at common/); release self-test must LOAD rule files — fa ticks red again

## Description

## Goal

Every gh-807 rules/query file shipped in an agents release must load cleanly in the pack runtime — the release self-test must LOAD all rule files (not just check pack zip contents), because rule requires resolve against the PACK's js/ root, not the source tree.

## Subject

The gh-807 verdict-reconciliation rules shipped in `agents-rel-20261009-124928` (and 143148). Symptom (fa, live): ticks fail with

```
❌ state query failed: Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js (JavaScript file not found in resources or filesystem: /home/runner/.dmtools/packs/sm_github-0.1.38/js/reviewVerdicts.js)
```

while the pack zip itself is correct (`js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` exists; `smAgent.js` correctly requires `./common/reviewVerdicts.js`). The flat `require('./reviewVerdicts.js')` lives in a **rules/query file from the agents tree**: when the tick loads rules into the pack runtime, `.` resolves to the pack's `js/` root → module miss.

- Fix: the rule file's require → `./common/reviewVerdicts.js` (pack-root-relative), consistent with smAgent.js.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: the offending rule file requires the module by its pack-resolvable path.
2. AC2: release self-test loads all rule files in the pack runtime; a wrong-path require fails the release (test: reintroduce the flat require locally → self-test red).
3. AC3: fa ticks green on `latest` (unpinned) for 3 consecutive ticks after the fix release.

- L1: rule-loader unit test with pack-runtime path resolution.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.)
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

+ * output. [paths] is any iterable of zip-layout paths (array or Set).

+    var out = [];
+    var seen = {};
+    var push = function (p) {
+        if (!p || seen[p]) return;

+        '// Requires every packed .js in the REAL dmtools runtime; any load or',
+        '// parse failure fails the release (the runner exits non-zero).',
+        'var FILES = ' + JSON.stringify(files) + ';',
+        'var required = 0;',
+        'var failed = [];',
+        'for (var i = 0; i < FILES.length; i++) {',
+        '    try {',
+        '        require(FILES[i]);',
+        '        required += 1;',
+        '    } catch (e) {',
+        '        failed.push(FILES[i] + " :: " + (e && e.message ? e.message : e));',
+        '    }',
+        '}',
+        'function action() {',
+        '    console.log("[pack-load-probe] required " + required + " module(s), " +',
+        '        failed.length + " failed");',

+        '        throw new Error("pack runtime load self-test FAILED: " +',
+        '            failed.length + " module(s) did not load");',
+        '    }',
+        '    if (required === 0) {',
+        '        throw new Error("pack runtime load self-test FAILED: no .js required");',
+        '    }',
+        '    return { success: true, required: required };',
+        '}',
+    ];
+    return lines.join('\n') + '\n';

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 824
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/824
- **Title**: gh-823 [BUG][P1] gh-807 rules require './reviewVerdicts.js' — fails in pack runtime (module lives at common/) release self-test must LOAD rule files — fa ticks red again
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-823` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 23
- **Additions**: +1053
- **Deletions**: -50
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T17:24:42Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T17:24:42Z

## PR Description

Closes #823
### Root Cause

The fa ticks died with `Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js (…/packs/sm_github-0.1.38/js/reviewVerdicts.js)` whenever a conflict-shaped gh-807 query had candidates. The dmtools runtime resolves requires **by execution time** (verified with a scratch probe pack): a require that runs while a module initializes resolves **file-relative**, but a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call) resolves against the **pack's `js/` root exclusively** — a file-relative hit is never tried. The lazy `require('./reviewVerdicts.js')` in `js/common/smProvider.js` (`_verdictRecordsModule`, fired by the `latestVerdict`/`notLatestVerdict` query guards) only executed in the deferred mode → `js/reviewVerdicts.js` → miss → whole tick red. Ticks without conflict-shaped candidates never ran it — hence the intermittent four-red-ticks pattern. Five more files carried the same latent shape (`./trackers.js` fallbacks in `jiraHelpers`/`tokenUsageComment`/`validateInputJql`/`contentOutput`, deferred `../configLoader.js` in `contentOutput`). The gh-812 zip-content gate passed the release because its union model assumed the runtime also tries the file-relative base for deferred requires — it does not.

### Fix

- Hoisted every deferred require to **load time** (file-relative — the mode where the spec is correct, and what `dmtools compile` discovers for the pack closure): `js/common/smProvider.js`, `jiraHelpers.js`, `tokenUsageComment.js`, `validateInputJql.js`, `contentOutput.js`.
- The ticket's literal pack-root-relative spec (`./common/reviewVerdicts.js`) is unshippable: `dmtools compile` resolves strictly file-relative and hard-fails the build on it (verified). Installer/compiler changes are a non-goal (#375), so eliminating the deferred mode is the only shape that compiles, loads, and keeps the closure complete.
- `ci/pack_require_gate.cjs`: the release require gate now classifies each literal require as **load-time** (union of bases, unchanged) vs **deferred** (function body → js-root base **only**). Reintroducing the shipped lazy require fails the release (AC2).
- `ci/pack_load_probe.cjs` + `assertPackLoads` in `ci/release_packs.mjs`: after every pack build the zip is extracted and a generated probe **requires every packed `.js` in the real dmtools runtime** — parse errors and load-time misses fail the release.
- `AGENTS.md`: the require-timing model documented as a coding constraint.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` (new): pins the resolution model, asserts the incident modules carry **zero deferred requires** (a re-lazied require turns it red), replays the verdict-record chain end-to-end through the provider.
- `js/unit-tests/test_packRequireGate.js`: deferred-require suites incl. the red-team replay of the shipped flat require → gate red; the pre-fix tree flags exactly the 8 shipped deferred requires, the fixed tree 0.
- `js/unit-tests/test_packLoadProbe.js` (new): the generated probe's selection/reporting/throw behavior.
- Full suite: **2213 passed, 0 failed**. Real-pack e2e: `sm_github` pack builds, static gate clean, runtime LOAD probe `required 18 module(s), 0 failed`; reintroduced flat require → gate red; corrupted module → probe red.

### Notes

- No behavior change beyond failure modes: the hoisted modules are pure and already load in every SM tick; `contentOutput`'s dropped `configLoader || require(...)` fallback was provably unreachable when the top-level holder resolved (same file, single path) and stays fail-open otherwise.
- AC3 (3 green ticks on unpinned `latest`) is operational and requires the fix release to ship — the release pipeline now runs both self-tests on every pack before publish.

# gh-823: [BUG][P1] gh-807 rules require './reviewVerdicts.js' — fails in pack runtime (module lives at common/); release self-test must LOAD rule files — fa ticks red again

## Description

## Goal

Every gh-807 rules/query file shipped in an agents release must load cleanly in the pack runtime — the release self-test must LOAD all rule files (not just check pack zip contents), because rule requires resolve against the PACK's js/ root, not the source tree.

## Subject

The gh-807 verdict-reconciliation rules shipped in `agents-rel-20261009-124928` (and 143148). Symptom (fa, live): ticks fail with

```
❌ state query failed: Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js (JavaScript file not found in resources or filesystem: /home/runner/.dmtools/packs/sm_github-0.1.38/js/reviewVerdicts.js)
```

while the pack zip itself is correct (`js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` exists; `smAgent.js` correctly requires `./common/reviewVerdicts.js`). The flat `require('./reviewVerdicts.js')` lives in a **rules/query file from the agents tree**: when the tick loads rules into the pack runtime, `.` resolves to the pack's `js/` root → module miss.

**Why intermittent (insidious):** the require executes only when a conflict-shaped query MATCHES. 12:56Z tick: no conflict → green. 16:2xZ ticks: fleet of approved/validated PRs + rework labels → match → every tick red. Four consecutive failed ticks 16:0x–16:2xZ.

## Capability surface

- Fix: the rule file's require → `./common/reviewVerdicts.js` (pack-root-relative), consistent with smAgent.js.
- Release self-test (extends #812): after pack build, LOAD every rule/query file in the pack runtime context — any require/parse failure fails the release. Zip-content checks alone cannot catch this class (the module EXISTS in the zip; the path from the caller is wrong).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: the offending rule file requires the module by its pack-resolvable path.
2. AC2: release self-test loads all rule files in the pack runtime; a wrong-path require fails the release (test: reintroduce the flat require locally → self-test red).
3. AC3: fa ticks green on `latest` (unpinned) for 3 consecutive ticks after the fix release.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-loader unit test with pack-runtime path resolution.
- L2: replay: rules from 124928 + pack 0.1.38 → loader must flag the flat require.
- L3 (live): fa unpin + 3 green ticks.

## Non-goals

- Installer-side changes (epam/dmtools-dart #375).
- Zombie mutex rule (#821) — separate, already assigned.

## References

- Incident 2 of the day: fa ticks red 16:0x–16:3xZ; mitigation pins `[REDACTED:High Entropy String]` + `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=.../124928` (both verified green 16:34Z, processed 7).

+ *
+ * The gh-812 require gate is a STATIC scan; gh-823 proved a second class it

+    var seen = {};
+    var push = function (p) {

+        if (p.indexOf('.js') !== p.length - 3) return;

+        'var FILES = ' + JSON.stringify(files) + ';',
+        'var required = 0;',
+        'var failed = [];',
+        'for (var i = 0; i < FILES.length; i++) {',
+        '    try {',
+        '        require(FILES[i]);',
+        '        required += 1;',
+        '    } catch (e) {',
+        '        failed.push(FILES[i] + " :: " + (e && e.message ? e.message : e));',

+        '            failed.length + " module(s) did not load");',
+        '    }',
+        '    if (required === 0) {',
+        '        throw new Error("pack runtime load self-test FAILED: no .js required");',
+        '    }',
+        '    return { success: true, required: required };',
+        '}',

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.)
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `…

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality

BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 824
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/824
- **Title**: gh-823 [BUG][P1] gh-807 rules require './reviewVerdicts.js' — fails in pack runtime (module lives at common/) release self-test must LOAD rule files — fa ticks red again
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-823` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 23
- **Additions**: +1053
- **Deletions**: -50
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T17:24:42Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T17:24:42Z

## PR Description

Closes #823
### Root Cause

The fa ticks died with `Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js (…/packs/sm_github-0.1.38/js/reviewVerdicts.js)` whenever a conflict-shaped gh-807 query had candidates. The dmtools runtime resolves requires **by execution time** (verified with a scratch probe pack): a require that runs while a module initializes resolves **file-relative**, but a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call) resolves against the **pack's `js/` root exclusively** — a file-relative hit is never tried. The lazy `require('./reviewVerdicts.js')` in `js/common/smProvider.js` (`_verdictRecordsModule`, fired by the `latestVerdict`/`notLatestVerdict` query guards) only executed in the deferred mode → `js/reviewVerdicts.js` → miss → whole tick red. Ticks without conflict-shaped candidates never ran it — hence the intermittent four-red-ticks pattern. Five more files carried the same latent shape (`./trackers.js` fallbacks in `jiraHelpers`/`tokenUsageComment`/`validateInputJql`/`contentOutput`, deferred `../configLoader.js` in `contentOutput`). The gh-812 zip-content gate passed the release because its union model assumed the runtime also tries the file-relative base for deferred requires — it does not.

### Fix

- Hoisted every deferred require to **load time** (file-relative — the mode where the spec is correct, and what `dmtools compile` discovers for the pack closure): `js/common/smProvider.js`, `jiraHelpers.js`, `tokenUsageComment.js`, `validateInputJql.js`, `contentOutput.js`.
- The ticket's literal pack-root-relative spec (`./common/reviewVerdicts.js`) is unshippable: `dmtools compile` resolves strictly file-relative and hard-fails the build on it (verified). Installer/compiler changes are a non-goal (#375), so eliminating the deferred mode is the only shape that compiles, loads, and keeps the closure complete.
- `ci/pack_require_gate.cjs`: the release require gate now classifies each literal require as **load-time** (union of bases, unchanged) vs **deferred** (function body → js-root base **only**). Reintroducing the shipped lazy require fails the release (AC2).
- `ci/pack_load_probe.cjs` + `assertPackLoads` in `ci/release_packs.mjs`: after every pack build the zip is extracted and a generated probe **requires every packed `.js` in the real dmtools runtime** — parse errors and load-time misses fail the release.
- `AGENTS.md`: the require-timing model documented as a coding constraint.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` (new): pins the resolution model, asserts the incident modules carry **zero deferred requires** (a re-lazied require turns it red), replays the verdict-record chain end-to-end through the provider.
- `js/unit-tests/test_packRequireGate.js`: deferred-require suites incl. the red-team replay of the shipped flat require → gate red; the pre-fix tree flags exactly the 8 shipped deferred requires, the fixed tree 0.
- `js/unit-tests/test_packLoadProbe.js` (new): the generated probe's selection/reporting/throw behavior.
- Full suite: **2213 passed, 0 failed**. Real-pack e2e: `sm_github` pack builds, static gate clean, runtime LOAD probe `required 18 module(s), 0 failed`; reintroduced flat require → gate red; corrupted module → probe red.

### Notes

- No behavior change beyond failure modes: the hoisted modules are pure and already load in every SM tick; `contentOutput`'s dropped `configLoader || require(...)` fallback was provably unreachable when the top-level holder resolved (same file, single path) and stays fail-open otherwise.
- AC3 (3 green ticks on unpinned `latest`) is operational and requires the fix release to ship — the release pipeline now runs both self-tests on every pack before publish.

# gh-823: [BUG][P1] gh-807 rules require './reviewVerdicts.js' — fails in pack runtime (module lives at common/); release self-test must LOAD rule files — fa ticks red again

## Description

## Goal

Every gh-807 rules/query file shipped in an agents release must load cleanly in the pack runtime — the release self-test must LOAD all rule files (not just check pack zip contents), because rule requires resolve against the PACK's js/ root, not the source tree.

## Subject

The gh-807 verdict-reconciliation rules shipped in `agents-rel-20261009-124928` (and 143148). Symptom (fa, live): ticks fail with

```
❌ state query failed: Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js (JavaScript file not found in resources or filesystem: /home/runner/.dmtools/packs/sm_github-0.1.38/js/reviewVerdicts.js)
```

while the pack zip itself is correct (`js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` exists; `smAgent.js` correctly requires `./common/reviewVerdicts.js`). The flat `require('./reviewVerdicts.js')` lives in a **rules/query file from the agents tree**: when the tick loads rules into the pack runtime, `.` resolves to the pack's `js/` root → module miss.

**Why intermittent (insidious):** the require executes only when a conflict-shaped query MATCHES. 12:56Z tick: no conflict → green. 16:2xZ ticks: fleet of approved/validated PRs + rework labels → match → every tick red. Four consecutive failed ticks 16:0x–16:2xZ.

## Capability surface

- Fix: the rule file's require → `./common/reviewVerdicts.js` (pack-root-relative), consistent with smAgent.js.
- Release self-test (extends #812): after pack build, LOAD every rule/query file in the pack runtime context — any require/parse failure fails the release. Zip-content checks alone cannot catch this class (the module EXISTS in the zip; the path from the caller is wrong).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: the offending rule file requires the module by its pack-resolvable path.
2. AC2: release self-test loads all rule files in the pack runtime; a wrong-path require fails the release (test: reintroduce the flat require locally → self-test red).
3. AC3: fa ticks green on `latest` (unpinned) for 3 consecutive ticks after the fix release.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-loader unit test with pack-runtime path resolution.
- L2: replay: rules from 124928 + pack 0.1.38 → loader must flag the flat require.
- L3 (live): fa unpin + 3 green ticks.

## Non-goals

- Installer-side changes (epam/dmtools-dart #375).
- Zombie mutex rule (#821) — separate, already assigned.

- Incident 2 of the day: fa ticks red 16:0x–16:3xZ; mitigation pins `[REDACTED:High Entropy String]` + `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=.../124928` (both verified green 16:34Z, processed 7).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.)
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.

+'use strict';
+/**
+ * Pack runtime LOAD self-test generator (gh-823, extends the gh-812 gate).
+ *
+ * The gh-812 require gate is a STATIC scan; gh-823 proved a second class it
+ * cannot see: code whose DEFERRED requires resolve against a different base
+ * than its load-time ones. This module generates the probe that loads every
+ * packed .js in the REAL dmtools runtime after the zip is built — any
+ * require/parse failure at load fails the release (the caller runs
+ * `dmtools run` on the generated config inside the extracted pack and
+ * treats a non-zero exit as a failed release).
+ *
+ * Pure string/JSON generation — no fs, no exec: the caller
+ * (ci/release_packs.mjs) owns the zip walk and the dmtools invocation, the
+ * same split as pack_require_gate.cjs. Unit-testable in the dmtools runner.
+ *
+ * The probe itself is authored for the pack runtime's rules (see
+ * test_packRequirePath.js): the generated file IS the main script, so its
+ * own `require`s resolve against the pack's js/ root, and every REQUIRED
+ * module gets the runtime's real init-time (file-relative) semantics.
+ * Deferred requires do not fire at load — that class stays with the static
+ * deferred-require gate; this probe catches parse errors and load-time
+ * resolution misses in the exact runtime the fa ticks will run.
+ */
+
+/**
+ * The js paths the probe will require: every packed .js except the probe
+ * itself (which is generated into the pack root). Sorted for deterministic
+ * output. [paths] is any iterable of zip-layout paths (array or Set).
+ */
+function probeFilesList(paths, probeName) {
+    var out = [];
+    var seen = {};
+    var push = function (p) {
+        if (!p || seen[p]) return;
+        seen[p] = true;
+        if (p === probeName) return;
+        if (p.indexOf('.js') !== p.length - 3) return;
+        if (p.indexOf('js/') !== 0) return;
+        out.push(p);
+    };
+    var add = typeof paths.forEach === 'function'
+        ? function (arr) { arr.forEach(push); }
+        : function (obj) { for (var k in obj) push(k); };
+    add(paths);
+    return out.sort();
+}
+
+/** The generated probe source: requires every file, reports, throws. */
+function renderProbeJs(files) {
+    var lines = [
+        '// GENERATED by ci/pack_load_probe.cjs — pack runtime load self-test (gh-823).',
+        '// Requires every packed .js in the REAL dmtools runtime; any load or',
+        '// parse failure fails the release (the runner exits non-zero).',
+        'var FILES = ' + JSON.stringify(files) + ';',
+        'var required = 0;',
+        'var failed = [];',
+        'for (var i = 0; i < FILES.length; i++) {',
+        '    try {',
+        '        require(FILES[i]);',
+        '        required += 1;',
+        '    } catch (e) {',
+        '        failed.push(FILES[i] + " :: " + (e && e.message ? e.message : e));',
+        '    }',
+        '}',
+        'function action() {',
+        '    console.log("[pack-load-probe] required " + required + " module(s), " +',
+        '        failed.length + " failed");',
+        '    for (var j = 0; j < failed.length; j++) console.log("  ❌ " + failed[j]);',
+        '    if (failed.length > 0) {',
+        '        throw new Error("pack runtime load self-test FAILED: " +',
+        '            failed.length + " module(s) did not load");',
+        '    }',
+        '    if (required === 0) {',
+        '        throw new Error("pack runtime load self-test FAILED: no .js required");',
+        '    }',
+        '    return { success: true, required: required };',
+        '}',
+    ];
+    return lines.join('\n') + '\n';
+}
+
+/** The generated JSRunner config pointing at the probe. */
+function renderProbeConfig(jsPath) {
+    return JSON.stringify({
+        name: 'JSRunner',
+        params: {
+            jsPath: jsPath,
+            jobParams: {}
+        }
+    }, null, 2) + '\n';
+}
+
+module.exports = {
+    probeFilesList: probeFilesList,
+    renderProbeJs: renderProbeJs,
+    renderProbeConfig: renderProbeConfig,
+};

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. The dmtools runtime resolves requires **by execution time** (verified with a scratch probe pack): a require that runs while a module initializes resolves **file-relative**, but a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call) resolves against the **pack's `js/` root exclusively** — a file-relative hit is never tried. The lazy `require('./reviewVerdicts.js')` in `js/common/smProvider.js` (`_verdictRecordsModule`, fired by the `latestVerdict`/`notLatestVerdict` query guards) only executed in the deferred mode → `js/reviewVerdicts.js` → miss → whole tick red. Ticks without conflict-shaped candidates never ran it — hence the intermittent four-red-ticks pattern. Five more files carried the same latent shape (`./trackers.js` fallbacks in `jiraHelpers`/`tokenUsageComment`/`validateInputJql`/`contentOutput`, deferred `../configLoader.js` in `contentOutput`). The gh-812 zip-content gate passed the release because its union model assumed the runtime also tries the file-relative base for deferred requires — it does not.

### Fix

- Hoisted every deferred require to **load time** (file-relative — the mode where the spec is correct, and what `dmtools compile` discovers for the pack closure): `js/common/smProvider.js`, `jiraHelpers.js`, `tokenUsageComment.js`, `validateInputJql.js`, `contentOutput.js`.
- The ticket's literal pack-root-relative spec (`./common/reviewVerdicts.js`) is unshippable: `dmtools compile` resolves strictly file-relative and hard-fails the build on it (verified). Installer/compiler changes are a non-goal (#375), so eliminating the deferred mode is the only shape that compiles, loads, and keeps the closure complete.
- `ci/pack_require_gate.cjs`: the release require gate now classifies each literal require as **load-time** (union of bases, unchanged) vs **deferred** (function body → js-root base **only**). Reintroducing the shipped lazy require fails the release (AC2).
- `ci/pack_load_probe.cjs` + `assertPackLoads` in `ci/release_packs.mjs`: after every pack build the zip is extracted and a generated probe **requires every packed `.js` in the real dmtools runtime** — parse errors and load-time misses fail the release.
- `AGENTS.md`: the require-timing model documented as a coding constraint.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` (new): pins the resolution model, asserts the incident modules carry **zero deferred requires** (a re-lazied require turns it red), replays the verdict-record chain end-to-end through the provider.
- `js/unit-tests/test_packRequireGate.js`: deferred-require suites incl. the red-team replay of the shipped flat require → gate red; the pre-fix tree flags exactly the 8 shipped deferred requires, the fixed tree 0.
- `js/unit-tests/test_packLoadProbe.js` (new): the generated probe's selection/reporting/throw behavior.
- Full suite: **2213 passed, 0 failed**. Real-pack e2e: `sm_github` pack builds, static gate clean, runtime LOAD probe `required 18 module(s), 0 failed`; reintroduced flat require → gate red; corrupted module → probe red.

### Notes

- No behavior change beyond failure modes: the hoisted modules are pure and already load in every SM tick; `contentOutput`'s dropped `configLoader || require(...)` fallback was provably unreachable when the top-level holder resolved (same file, single path) and stays fail-open otherwise.
- AC3 (3 green ticks on unpinned `latest`) is operational and requires the fix release to ship — the release pipeline now runs both self-tests on every pack before publish.

## Description

## Goal

Every gh-807 rules/query file shipped in an agents release must load cleanly in the pack runtime — the release self-test must LOAD all rule files (not just check pack zip contents), because rule requires resolve against the PACK's js/ root, not the source tree.

## Subject

The gh-807 verdict-reconciliation rules shipped in `agents-rel-20261009-124928` (and 143148). Symptom (fa, live): ticks fail with

```

while the pack zip itself is correct (`js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` exists; `smAgent.js` correctly requires `./common/reviewVerdicts.js`). # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.)
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

+'use strict';
+/**
+ * Pack runtime LOAD self-test generator (gh-823, extends the gh-812 gate).
+ *
